atAGlance: Bún cá is fish noodle soup, usually with fried or fresh fish, dill or tomato, herbs, and rice vermicelli.
whatItIs: Bún cá is fish noodle soup, often with fried fish pieces or fresh fish in a bright broth with tomato, dill, herbs, and rice vermicelli. It feels lighter than beef noodle soups but still deeply savory.
howToEnjoy: Check for bones before your first big bite, then season with lime and chili slowly. Herbs brighten the fish broth, while too much chili can cover the seafood sweetness.
howLocalsOrder: Order bún cá by the full name and ask whether bones remain if you are worried about bones. Start with the broth plain, then add herbs, lime, and chili after you understand the shop style.
worthKnowing: Bún cá often feels coastal or northern on a menu, and each city handles the fish differently: crisp fried pieces, softer fillets, tomato brightness, or dill fragrance.
goodToKnow: Fish bones can appear, especially in more traditional bowls.
